entries.title: The Best Prime Day Apple Deals (2026) Are About to Expire
entries.summary: MacBooks, iPads, AirPods, and just about every Apple accessory imaginable are on sale for Prime Day—but only hours remain.
entries.content:
Amazon Prime Day is one of the easiest times of year to save on Apple devices. Many Apple gadgets go on sale often, but Prime Day Apple deals frequently drop prices down to as low as we’ve seen—if not exceeding previous best discounts entirely.

You won’t find deals on the brand-new iPhone, but if you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple Watches, iPads, MacBooks, and third-party accessories, you’re in the right spot. But only hours remain as Prime Day comes to a close, so jump on it quick.

For more savings, be sure to check out all the Absolute Best Prime Day Deals we've found so far.

Updated 10:00 pm ET October 7: We've added a new deal and double-checked the existing discounts. Sign up for Prime here to unlock exclusive deals.

WIRED Featured Deals

  • The AirPods deal you’ve been waiting for: AirPods Pro 3 for $179 ($70 off)
  • The best MacBook deal: MacBook Air M5 for $1,099 ($200 off)
  • The best impulse buy: Anker Nano Power Bank for $20 ($7 off)
  • The best mobile controller for your iPhone: Backbone One for $64 ($16 off)
  • The best MagSafe wallet: Smartish Side Hustle Wallet for $23 ($12 off)

Best Apple Device Deals

The Apple AirPods Pro 3 are the best wireless earbuds for iPhone users. They fall to this price quite frequently, but WIRED readers continually purchase them, and this deal is still better than paying full price. They have detailed sound, great noise cancellation and transparency modes, a built-in heart rate sensor, and live translation.

The AirPods Max 2 are sleek, stylish, and on sale for a match of the second-best deal we've seen. They've dropped to $399 a couple of times, but this deal is still worth considering if these are the headphones you want. The battery life could be better, and we wish there were custom EQ options, but we like them overall.

The Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 are some of our favorite workout earbuds thanks to their comfortable fit, appealing style, and punchy sound. They’ll stay put even if you’re sweaty, and the transparency mode and noise cancellation mean you can hear exactly as much of your surroundings as you want to.

The MacBook Air remains the best laptop we’d recommend for most people. It strikes a great balance of features, power, and price, offering enough performance for both work and play. The portable, sleek design and excellent battery life make it an easy recommendation for just about anybody. And in terms of price, this is the best deal we’ve seen on the M5 MacBook Air since June.

The standard 11-inch iPad avoided a price hike this year and remains a great tablet for families. It’s perfect for kicking back with a movie, game, or book, and it can be relied upon to keep the kids amused.

The new M6 Mac Mini is very fast and can easily serve as a local, agentic AI machine. But it also has a more mainstream appeal as a starter computer, complete with 16 GB of RAM, the powerful M6 chip, and 512 GB of storage. Amazon has the best deal on the very latest model, bringing the price to a new low since its release. The Mac Studio is also on sale, if you really want to dive in deep on running local AI models.

These are the best trackers for folks with an iPhone, and you can use them to keep tabs on your keys, travel luggage, bike, or whatever else you worry might go missing. The location of each AirTag is marked clearly in the Find My app. They also make great stocking stuffers.

The GPS-only version of this Apple Watch is a very solid deal if you don't need cellular connectivity or the large band. The Apple Watch SE is our top budget-friendly pick; it costs less than the higher-end models but leaves out some of their features. I'm surprised that every version isn't discounted, but we hope to see other configurations drop in price over the event.

Unlike the Magic Mouse, Apple's Magic Keyboard is a beloved Mac accessory. Mechanical switch enthusiasts won't appreciate the shallow travel, but the tick-tack typing of the keyboard makes it a fast and comfortable keyboard to type on. And importantly, it gives you the macOS layout right out of the box. The non-Touch ID model is on sale for Prime Day, which makes it $70 cheaper than the version with a fingerprint reader.

Best MagSafe and Accessory Deals

As Apple purges the ports on its MacBooks, you might want to plug in a handy USB hub. This Plugable device is our favorite because it offers 140 watts of power delivery, every port you need, including 10-Gbps USB-C, and can support a secondary screen, up to 4K resolution at 60 Hz. It also boasts a robust metal chassis with clearly labeled ports.

I loved the Backbone One when I reviewed it, and I still think it’s the best mobile gaming controller. It makes it very easy to play games on my iPhone for hours at a time. I especially love it for traveling, whether on a plane or to my parents’ house for the holidays. It has a solid app and excellent controls, plus pass-through charging. This price is close to the best we’ve seen.

This slots into the bottom of your iPhone via the rotating USB-C connector and provides enough power to charge it up at least once. It’s a good alternative to a MagSafe power bank if you want something faster and more efficient than wireless charging.

The best MagSafe power bank has a built-in kickstand and can charge your phone wirelessly or via the included USB-C cable. The capacity isn’t massive, but it’ll still fully charge most phones at least once. The display lets you know how much juice is left at a quick glance.

Top pick in our guide to the best Apple 3-in-1 wireless chargers, this classy-looking tree has a lovely weighted base and spots to charge your iPhone (with support for StandBy mode), Apple Watch, and any AirPods with a wireless charging case.

This is the best Apple 3-in-1 travel charger because it is so compact when folded. It can charge your iPhone or Qi2-certified phone at up to 15 watts on a magnetic pad that can adjust to your preferred angle. A second pad charges AirPods or other wireless earbuds, and there is a fold-out Apple Watch charger.

This hard-wearing, fast-charging pick from the best USB-C cables can deliver 240 watts to charge any Apple gadget. It also has a tough, braided nylon exterior made from 100 percent recycled plastic, and comes with a lifetime warranty.

This neat little Apple 3-in-1 charger has space for your Apple Watch, AirPods, and iPhone (in any orientation, including StandBy mode). It also comes with a wall adapter, travel adapters, and a cable, all of which are unfortunately rare inclusions in this product space.

One of our favorite MagSafe wallets, the stylish Smartish Side Hustle clings to your iPhone magnetically and has a cutaway to make it easy to pop out your cards, saving time at the register. This price is the lowest we’ve seen.

I especially like the version of this MagSafe wallet that has Find My compatibility, but the basic version is good as well. Nearly every iteration is on sale. The wallet has space for two cards comfortably and can double as a kickstand or tripod for your daily fit checks.

Best Apple Case and Watch Band Deals

Bandolier’s elegant, classy products feel a lot more luxurious than most iPhone accessories. This case turns your iPhone 17 into a crossbody device, and I especially like it for dinner or shows when I don’t want to set my phone down, or my outfit doesn’t have pockets. My Bandolier accessories show no sign of wear after three months of continuous use.

Our favorite silicone Apple Watch band has a pebbled leather look, but it’s softer, and it’s waterproof. Durable enough for workouts and water sports, but also smart enough for the office, the two-tone design is reversible.

entries.title: Best October Prime Day Deals to Shop Before the Sale Ends (2026)
entries.summary: Amazon Prime Big Deal Days are here, and we’ve tracked down the best discounts on all the gear our team recommends.
entries.content:
Amazon’s fall Prime Day sale—also known as Big Deal Days 2026—is in its final hours. The sale started yesterday, October 6, and runs through midnight tonight, so don't wait if there's something you wanted to buy on sale. As with all Prime Day sales, you'll need to be an Amazon Prime member to take advantage of the discounts.

Apple Mac Mini (M6) $ 899 $ 780

It may only be October, but it's never too early to jump on that holiday gift shopping. We've combed through all the deals and found the best ones, based on our years of testing and reviewing. WIRED's picks for the best Prime Day deals only include products someone from our team has personally tested and reviewed. We track prices using several tools to avoid falling for fake discounts. There are no shoddy knockoffs or overpriced products among our recommendations, just good deals on great gear that we personally use ourselves.

WIRED Featured Deals

  • The best MacBook deal: MacBook Air M5 for $1,099 ($200 off)
  • The AirPods Pro 3 deal you’ve been waiting for: AirPods Pro 3 for $179 ($70 off)
  • A walking pad for your fitness goals: Urevo CyberPad for Home for $368 ($112 off)
  • A colorful Kindle for less: Kindle Colorsoft for $190 ($100 off)
  • The best impulse buy: TP-Link Tapo Matter-Certified Smart Plug Mini for $19 ($6 Off)
  • A subscription-less digital calendar: Everblog HomeCal Calendar for $280 ($120 off)
  • The best robot vacuum: Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal for $750 ($550 off)
  • An automatic espresso machine at an all-time low: De'Longhi Rivelia for $1,000 ($300 off)

Updated 9:30 pm ET October 7: We've added a fresh batch of new deals, removed some dead deals, and confirmed accurate pricing. Sign up for Prime here to unlock exclusive deals.

Contributors: Louryn Strampe, Simon Hill, Nena Farrell, Kat Merck, Molly Higgins, Boutayna Chokrane, Luke Larsen, Harry Rabinowitz, Les Shu

Best Apple Deals

As someone who’s tested dozens of laptops this year already, I still find myself recommending the MacBook Air M5 more than any other. It’s the most well-rounded laptop you can buy, sporting great performance, long battery life, and a razor-thin chassis. The price has gone up considerably over the past year, but that’s true of many of the best laptops. And now, it's at its lowest price since June, making it an absolute must-buy and the top of my list for Prime Day laptop deals. —Luke Larsen

Apple AirPods Pro 3 are the best wireless earbuds for anyone with an iPhone. They’ve got best-in-class noise-canceling, an excellent transparency mode, clear and detailed audio quality, and a plethora of advanced features like built-in heart rate sensors and live translation. The heart rate sensors are particularly impressive—you can go on a run with just your phone and these earbuds and get accurate GPS, heart rate zone, and calorie data. —Harry Rabinowitz

The Mac Mini has been sold out for the majority of this year due to the rapid escalation of interest in using them as local, agentic AI machines. The brand-new M6 model is faster (and more expensive) than ever. But the fact that you can buy them at all right now feels significant, and Amazon has the best deal on the latest model you’ll find. —Luke Larsen

Apple AirPods Max 2 are the best over-ear headphones for anyone with an iPhone, MacBook, and other Apple staples. They have some of the best sound quality, noise-canceling, and transparency modes of any headphone out there. They are pricey, but $120 off sticker price makes them more in-line with options from Sony and Bose.—Harry Rabinowitz

Best Kindle Deals

While almost all of Amazon's Kindles are on sale, the Colorsoft is one of the best. While it was also hit with a price hike at the end of August, with the base model rising to $290 from $250, you can get it for $100 off during Amazon's sale. It has everything we like about the Paperwhite, but with a color screen (and now with Dark Mode, which it originally lacked!). For only $20 more during Amazon Big Deal Days, I'd get the Colorsoft over the Paperwhite. —Nena Farrell

If you're looking to get the biggest discount on a new Kindle, the best sale is on the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft. It's got an 11-inch color screen and comes with a stylus to let it double as a digital notebook. It's the most expensive Kindle, but it also has the best discount during Amazon's sale event. —Nena Farrell

The most affordable Kindle is the 11th-gen base Kindle, but it's not as cheap as it used to be. It used to dip below $100 at these sale events, but Amazon raised prices for most Kindle models, so now this might be the best price we see going forward. While I'm not happy about it, I'd recommend getting it on sale versus waiting for it to go up even higher. —Nena Farrell

If you're bummed that there's no Kindle under $100 during Prime Day anymore, I have a solution for you. The Xteink X4 Pro Pocket E-Reader is a tiny e-reader with just a 4.3-inch display that fits in the palm of your hand (or your pocket!) It's easy to use, and you can send web pages and articles to it easily through the app. It doesn't have a built-in store, though, so it's harder to get ebooks onto it. —Nena Farrell

The Best Headphone Deals

This is the lowest price ever for the Nothing Headphone (1), an excellent, stylish pair of over-ear headphones with great sound and even better battery life: up to 35 hours with noise-canceling on or 80 hours with it off. The headphones have tactile controls on each earcup I personally love—things like a volume wheel, Bluetooth pairing button, on-off switch, and media control paddle. —Harry Rabinowitz

Best Smart Home Deals

Amazon launched two new Echo Show smart displays last year, and the Echo Show 11 was easily the better of the two. The sound is better, and the screen is larger—but not so large that it's a pain to put on a kitchen counter. Amazon did raise the price by $30 at the end of August, but this is still the lowest deal price I've seen for it since its launch. —Nena Farrell

The Echo Studio has been our favorite Echo speaker for the sound quality since the original model, and the second-generation version packs fantastic sound like its predecessor. I also love that its price didn't increase between the two generations, or after Amazon's price hike in August. It's still one of the more expensive models, even on sale, so I'd choose it only if you have a massive room you're trying to fill with sound. But it's also the only new Echo that didn't get a price increase, so this sale isn't just a trick of the numbers. —Nena Farrell

If you want a similar experience to the Skylight Calendar without worrying about the subscription fee, the Everblog HomeCal is the closest digital wall calendar I've found. It has a similar interface and menu options (calendar, meals, chores, etc) and allows you to set it up as a digital photo frame when you aren't using it. The photo upload tool is slower, but it's worth it to be free. —Nena Farrell

A good smart plug is handy all over the house. I really like this set from TP-Link's Tapo brand because the plugs are Matter-certified, making them easy to pair with any existing smart home ecosystem, and have a small form factor so they won't block the other outlets. I like them best for controlling lamps that don't fit for a smart bulb, but you could use them for all kinds of things. —Nena Farrell

If you want a really great, reliable automatic litter box but don’t need extras like AI recognition or an internal camera to watch, I think this is the best model. In fact, it’s the automatic litter box I recommend for most people. It’s an upgrade from the Petkit PuraMax 2 (which I also loved). It has a larger opening and better odor control than the previous model. It also has a connected app, where you can monitor usage and adjust settings from afar. At less than $400, this is a pretty cheap price point for a model of this caliber. —Molly Higgins

I’ve tested air purifiers that cost 10 times as much as this budget Levoit, but I keep coming back to this affordable pick. I really love the connected app, which lets me adjust settings like fan speed and modes from afar and check filter life. Plus, the app sends notifications when air quality is poor and updates when it reaches clean levels again. You can also see historical indoor air quality levels and the corresponding action the purifier took, which helps track patterns. It’s also compatible with Amazon Alexa or Google Assistant for voice control. —Molly Higgins

Laptop and Home Office Deals

With its OLED screen and a super-thin design, you'd never guess this laptop was as cheap as it is. The Qualcomm Snapdragon X chip inside is what makes it special though, offering great battery life and quiet performance. This particular deal gets you the 16-inch size with a full terabyte of storage (and 16 GB of RAM) for just $750. The touchpad is the main area where this laptop struggles and falls behind the MacBook Neo and Dell XPS 13. But the HP OmniBook 5 gets you extra memory and storage at a killer price. —Luke Larsen

When it comes to monitors, all most people need is something reliable, comfortable to use, and not horrifically ugly. That’s underselling the Dell S2725HSM, despite its price. It’s a basic 1080p resolution, but it has really solid image quality, and it even comes with a 144-Hz refresh rate. All those features are heightened when it’s on sale for just $130, too. That’s the biggest price drop I’ve seen on this monitor in a while. —Luke Larsen

Tilt-Pan-Zoom webcams like the Obsbot Tiny 3 are so much more than just a webcam for video calls. The gimbal gives the camera a huge range of motion, letting you dramatically expand what you can shoot compared to a standard webcam. It’s ideal for streamers, content creators, podcasters, and online educators—or really anyone who wants to show more of their room on video. On top of that, it also has tons of interesting AI features to play with. This is a rare discount on this top-shelf webcam, too. —Luke Larsen

On its own, this is a decent 4K webcam with all the typical high-end webcam trappings. But this one has a trick up its sleeve: Being able to easily switch between portrait and landscape. And because it magnetically attaches to the mount, it works just as well in both modes. For anyone shooting social videos, it’s extremely handy. —Luke Larsen

Your laptop probably doesn’t have all the ports you might need. I like this one because it matches a MacBook pretty nicely, and provides nine ports in one, providing everything from hard-wired Ethernet to an HDMI to support an external 4K display. It’s useful enough to just leave on your desk or toss in your bag on trips. The peace of mind of knowing you won’t run ever be caught off guard without the port you need is priceless.—Luke Larsen

This tri-band Wi-Fi 7 mesh is the best subscription-free mesh system for most people. A two-pack will be enough to cover most homes, and each router has two 10-Gbps Ethernet ports, one Gigabit port, and a USB 3.0 port. Asus allows you to tinker with and configure everything and offers comprehensive security software and parental controls at no extra cost (you can even redeem a free year of NordVPN service with this mesh). Clip the on-page coupon to save. —Simon Hill

Our current pick for the best Android tablet, the Galaxy Tab S10 FE comes in cheaper than the iPad despite having lots of advanced features. Most notably, it comes with the S Pen stylus bundled in, making it a a great notetaking device to take on the go. —Luke Larsen

Best AV Deals

This soundbar plus subwoofer is a fantastic way to upgrade your TV audio system for a reasonable price, especially at 25 percent off. The Polk Signa S4 is one of our favorite soundbars for that very reason: It’s simple, easy to use, sounds great, and doesn’t cost an arm and a leg. Sure, it doesn’t have more advanced features like Wi-Fi connectivity, voice assistant support, or multi-speaker surround sound. But if you’re coming from built-in TV speakers, this is a great first upgrade. —Harry Rabinowitz

Phone Deals

The best Samsung phones are on sale. If you want an Android phone with real power, but prefer something that’s not too big, the Samsung Galaxy S26 is tough to beat. It’s fast, has a bright and sharp screen, a reliable triple-camera system, and good battery life. You also get seven years of software support, and the base model has jumped to 256 GB of storage. This has been cheaper, but with prices on the rise across the market, I’m not sure when it will dip again. This is still a decent discount. —Simon Hill

The Google Pixel 11 is the value sweet spot in Google’s new lineup, especially with this hefty discount. It combines a great camera, strong battery life, and solid performance with Qi2 25W support and slick contextual AI features. —Simon Hill

Best Vacuum Deals

My all-time favorite robot vacuum is often on sale, but this is the lowest the price it ever goes (and used to only go as low as $800, so don't miss it!) The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal uses a UV light to spot stains and spills on your floor and will go back to scrub them away after doing its regular clean. It's the smartest one I've tried in 2026 by a long shot, and little announcements from the base station make it easy to know when the vacuum is just cleaning versus handling stains. —Nena Farrell

Roborock has been launching new robot vacuums left and right, particularly in its more affordable Qrevo line, and one of the best we've tested is the Qrevo Curv 2 Flow. It's a great vacuum with a roller mop and 20,000 Pa of suction, and its little base station feels sleek and painless to add to your home. —Nena Farrell

I usually see a lot of Dyson vacuums on sale during events like these, and the slightly older Dyson V15 is often one of them. Now that there are newer models, the V15's sale price is just under $600, and it's a good price for a Dyson vacuum that comes with both a hard floor and all-floor cleaner head, plus a crevice tool. There's an LCD screen too, which you won't find on Dyson's new, more affordable models. —Nena Farrell

Mobile Charging and Accessory Deals

Why settle for a dull black brick when you can snag translucent tech that looks like it came from a Cyberpunk world? This isn’t just the best-looking power bank, it’s also functionally awesome. It can supply up to 170 watts, has an ample 24,000-mAh capacity, and scores an IP66 rating for water resistance, meaning there’s no need to worry about rain. —Simon Hill

The Smartish Side Hustle is one of our favorite MagSafe wallets. These kinds of wallets can be tricky to use in daily life, but this wallet is designed to pop cards out for you, saving time at the register. This price is the best we've tracked. —Louryn Strampe

The Best TV Deals

An affordable OLED TV is rare, but this newly launched model from Sony is an exception during this sale. It's Sony's entry-level OLED TV, and while it might have fewer bells and whistles than the Sony Bravia 8 II, it's far easier on your wallet and still delivers a rich picture with deep black tones and excellent color contrast. It also has Google Gemini built in, which you can use to control the picture, change settings, flip inputs, and ask about obscure sci-fi movies from the ’70s. —John Brandon

This screen-free play stage and speaker for kids is enormous fun. Simply slot one of the wooden cartridges in the top and pop wooden character pieces on the circular soundstage, divided into four sections, to change the audio it plays. This basic functionality allows for a clever variety of themed add-on packs, including classical music and a cooking game.

Best Kitchen and Coffee Deals

If you’re looking to cut down on food waste but don’t want to deal with smelly compost containers and mess, FoodCycler 3 is one of my top picks for this purpose. Put your peels, cores, and wilted herbs into the included 3.5-liter countertop bucket; when it’s full, seat it right in the machine, which will then grind and dry your scraps to a fine powder. You can then top-dress your lawn with the resultant “Foodilizer,” put it in your yard waste bin, or even mix it with soil (1:10 ratio) to use in your garden. —Kat Merck

My parents bought this bread machine years ago because it was one of the only models with a ceramic pan and no suspicious nonstick coatings. They handed it down to me, and I still have it. It works flawlessly, turning out ball-shaped 1-, 1.5-, or 2-lb. loaves. It doesn’t have as much versatility as higher-end machines like the Zojirushi Virtuoso, which does a better job with specialty breads, but if you’re interested in making your own basic, preservative-free loaves without having to mess with starters, kneading, and all-day rising schedules, this machine is the best value out there. —Kat Merck

The Solo Stove Pi Prime is an excellent pizza oven, with an elegant and functional design that is more round than oval. It's propane-powered and has solid wind shielding, and it won't take up too much space in your backyard. —Louryn Strampe

This is a solid deal on the best automatic latte and cappuccino maker we've tested. The Rivelia is user-friendly and easy to use, and it even has a built-in milk frother in addition to the grinder. We also like the touchscreen display and consistently tasty results. —Louryn Strampe

Athletic Greens has a newer formula with a few additional ingredients, but the Classic formula is cheaper than we've seen before. This brand doesn't go on sale often. I noticed smoother digestion and higher energy levels when I tested this greens powder, which can be a beneficial way to supplement your diet in addition to whole fruits and veggies. —Louryn Strampe

Best Gaming Deals

I've tried many mobile gaming controllers, and the Backbone One remains the best. It feels great, it's fast and tactile, and the app makes finding new games easy. This price comes within $5 of the best we've seen. —Louryn Strampe

In the world of PC gaming, this keyboard truly qualifies as a classic. It’s a few years old at this point, but this wireless, mechanical gaming keyboard is extremely balanced and well-made. The tenkeyless layout gives you everything you need without overtaking your desk (or getting in the way of your mouse hand), and the design has some flash without overdoing it. —Luke Larsen

The Steelcase Gesture is our recommendation for a premium office chair. If you want something that feels a little more luxurious and cushy, it's a very safe bet. It still has several elegant points of adjustment and the foam seat is plush and comfortable. —Louryn Strampe

The Best Camera Deals

The wee little Lit Hero is GoPro's smallest, lightest, cheapest action camera. It's my favorite GoPro for selfies thanks to the included light. The cluster of four LEDs next to the lens ensures this camera keeps you well-lit in every scene. The Lit Hero isn't quite as capable video-wise as the Hero 13 Black (also on sale, see below), but it can shoot 4K at 60 fps, and the battery held up for a respectable 101 minutes during my test (shooting a 4K 60 fps video). —Scott Gilbertson

Health and Fitness Deals

The Theragun Relief is our budget Theragun pick, and during Prime Day, it’s an even cheaper buy. It’s an older 2023 model, but massage guns don’t need the latest features to be effective. You get three attachments and three speed settings, and it’s half the weight of the Pro Plus, making it much easier to pack for travel. I’ve seen the price drop even lower, but $120 is still a solid discount on one of our favorite percussive guns. —Boutayna Chokrane

The Theragun Mini Plus is our favorite portable massage gun. It’s not only compact and TSA-approved, but it also features heat therapy. At $238, it’s at the lowest price I’ve seen, making this the ideal time to snag one if you were considering it. The Mini Plus is also compatible with the Cold Plus and Vibration Plus attachments, which are both sold separately. —Boutayna Chokrane

Already the most affordable Apple Watch in the lineup, the SE 3 is the sleeper hit of the Apple Watch lineup. It's the most affordable (even more so on sale), yet it has many of the same day-to-day features of its pricier siblings, including an always on display, health and fitness tracking, and seamless syncing with your iPhone. —Harry Rabinowitz

Smart scales can be tough to justify when they cost hundreds of dollars, but $69 off makes our top pick even easier to recommend. The Withings Body Comp is among the most advanced smart scales we’ve tested, with a companion app that can track data for up to eight users. It’s also meant to last a lifetime; WIRED reviewer Christopher Null has Withings info dating back to 2010 and plans to keep the streak going. —Boutayna Chokrane

WIRED contributing reviewer Christopher Null has tried a lot of pool-cleaning robots, and this is his favorite. It offers flawless cleaning of your floors, walls, and waterline, plus an app and a battery with six hours of charge underwater. It also floats when it’s done, so you don’t have to fish it up from the bottom. The only downside—aside from its heft—is the price, but this is a genuinely good sale, so worth snagging at this price if you’ve been considering it. —Kat Merck

As someone who’s tested dozens of sets of packing cubes, I believe these to be the best you can buy on Amazon. Compression, label windows, lots of color options, breathability, privacy—this six-piece set has it all. This particular package gets you four rectangular cubes with handles, plus a shoe bag and double-open drawstring bag for dirty clothes or bulkier items. Everything you need for fitting the maximum amount in your carry-on. —Kat Merck

If you’re looking for the most reliable smart bird feeder at the best price, you won’t do better than Birdfy’s original plastic feeder. Birdfy recently surpassed 1 million units sold and continues to advance its app with new features, including the ability to identify multiple birds on a feeder at once. The plastic feeder body comes with blue or yellow accents and is a bit lightweight, so you’ll want to make sure to mount it away from squirrels who could damage it. This model comes with an auxiliary solar panel and has no paywalled subscription features, so you won’t have to stress about hidden post-purchase fees. —Kat Merck

Mine had black-capped chickadees, but the Duo comes with different sized holes (and corresponding metal predator guards to prevent chewing) to appeal to different species. You can also raise the floor up or down to change the cavity size. I wouldn’t recommend this in hot climates due to the black-painted side and lack of ventilation, but otherwise it’s a must-buy if you love birds. —Kat Merck

If you want to brighten up your holiday season, the Philips Hue Festavia are the best smart Christmas lights you can buy. This 65-foot string is easy to drape on an indoor or outdoor tree (the lights are IP54 rated) and sports 250 tiny LEDs. You can pick any color, animate with twinkly effects, and even tune white to find your preferred color temperature. Cozy and classy, these smart string lights can be scheduled with different colors or effects for different times of day, paired with other Hue lights, or synced with music. —Simon Hill

entries.title: The 28 Best Prime Day Tech Deals Will Expire Tonight
entries.summary: Never pay full price. Bag yourself some Prime Day tech deals on our favorite WIRED-tested gadgets before they disappear.
entries.content:
Amazon Prime Day ends tonight at midnight. Some of our favorite pieces of tech that we've tested from this year are on sale—some dropping to the lowest prices we've ever seen. That includes phones, laptops, headphones, cameras, tablets, and much more. These are all products we've tested ourselves and stand by in terms of quality and value.

But they won't last forever. You have until tonight to pull the trigger. If you haven’t found the deal you want yet, browse our roundup of the Absolute Best Prime Day Deals.

Updated on October 7 at 7:15 pm ET: Added some new tech deals and checked through the current products on sale.

  • Nothing’s Best Headphones: Nothing Headphone (1) for $189 ($110 Off)
  • Samsung’s Most Powerful Smartphone: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra for $980 ($420 Off)
  • Apple’s Rarely Discounted MacBook: Apple MacBook Air for $1,099 ($200 Off)
  • Eufy's Pan-and-Tilt Security Camera: Eufy EufyCam S4 Security Camera for $260 ($90 Off)
  • Samsung's Affordable Art TV: Samsung The Frame LS03F for $898 ($600 Off)

Sign up for Prime here to unlock exclusive deals.

Audio and TV Deals

The flagship Apple AirPods Pro 3 are its best wireless earbuds, and they're at the lowest price since June. Music sounds great, noise cancellation works well, and they offer excellent call quality. Apple added more ear tips for a better fit for small ears, new tools like heart rate sensing and live translation, and enhanced support for folks with hearing loss. If you use an iPhone, these are the wireless earbuds for you.

The Nothing Headphone (1) is one of our favorite pairs of over-ear headphones. With an attractive and distinctive design that combines a transparent look with tactile controls like a volume wheel and media control paddle, these headphones make a real statement. They also boast top-notch battery life. This is the best discount we’ve seen on them so far.

Prime Day is a great time to pick up older models at deep discounts. The Sonos Beam Gen 2 is a great example, having coming out originally in 2021. It's since been supplanted by the Sonos Beam Ultra, but that model is hundreds of dollars more (even while on sale!), and the Sonos Beam Gen 2 has never been cheaper. Our own audio expert, Harry Rabinowitz, used this model in his own home as his primary soundbar and found it to be a particularly good fit for smaller homes.

Speaking of deals on older models, if you've always fancied one of those picture-style TVs, this 2025 Samsung model has a matte finish to make paintings and photos look more real, for when you're not using it as a TV. The magnetic bezels are customizable, and some folks love the look. To be honest, these aren't best TVs, sadly, Amazon doesn't have any Prime Day deals on them.

It's rare to find a brand new OLED TV on this big of a discount, but that's exactly what this Bravia 6 deal is. While this is definitely Sony's entry-level OLED option, I'm still surprised to see this big of a price cut this early. We tested the Sony Bravia 8 II a few months back, which is this TV's “True RGB” older sibling, and while the Bravia 6 is missing some of those bells and whistles, it still delivers excellent color contrast and deep blacks where it counts.

Phones, Wearables, and Accessories Deals

Available in dazzling hibiscus, the Google Pixel 11 stands out, and also happens to be the best option in Google’s new lineup for most people. It boasts an excellent camera, long battery life, and decent performance, alongside Qi2 25W support for magnetic charging and accessories, and super slick contextual AI features.

The Samsung S26 Ultra was the pick of the bunch this year, with a cool privacy screen, blazing performance, long battery life, and an excellent camera, but all three of Samsung’s S26 phones are on sale right now. These are the lowest prices they’ve been so far.

The Moto G Stylus is our pick of the best cheap phones under $400, and is is as low as it has ever been right now. If you miss a headphone jack and microSD card slot, this could be a winner. This is the 2025 model, but Motorola increased the price by $100 for the 2026 Moto G Stylus, and, apart from the upgraded active stylus, there’s little to justify the extra cost.

The Google Pixel Watch 5 is the best smartwatch for Android phone owners. It tracks your activity, sleep, heart rate, and more automatically, and works seamlessly with Gemini. You can also get insights and coaching from Google Health if you subscribe.

This is a solid smartwatch, and an especially great choice if you have a Samsung Galaxy phone. You can save yourself a significant sum by opting for last year’s model and Samsung’s Galaxy Watch9 is only a modest upgrade over the Watch8, considering it’s $120 more expensive.

Anyone with a trio of Apple gadgets (iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods) will benefit from snagging one of the best Apple 3-in-1 wireless chargers for their nightstand, and this is my top pick. The wide base keeps it steady, enabling you to remove your iPhone from the magnetic wireless charging pad one-handed, the Watch pad lets any strap dangle, and the base has a spot for AirPods, too.

This power bank does it all. I love the translucent design, offering a peek at the electronic innards. It has a handy display with comprehensive stats, and it supports just about every fast charging protocol going. It packs 24,000 mAh of power and can charge at up to 140 watts, so it will juice up anything from a laptop down. It’s even IP66 rated for water and dust resistance.

Want a hard-wearing, fast charging cable to keep your gadgetry juiced? This Anker cable from the best USB-C cables is our pick. It can deliver 240 watts, has a tough, braided nylon exterior made from 100 percent recycled plastic, and comes with a lifetime warranty. Anker promises this cable will last a century and it can operate in temperatures from -40 degrees to 176 degrees Fahrenheit. The ribbed cuffs make it easy to grip, and it’s USB-IF certified, too.

Computers and Home Office Deals

The M5 MacBook Air got a serious price hike at the end of June, bringing it up to $1,299. But this week, everyone’s favorite laptop dropped to $1,099, which is the lowest price it’s been at in months. It comes with 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage, so you’re getting a really solid configuration that should last you many years. The 15-inch model is also $200 off if you need a larger screen to work on. Regardless, this is the best laptop can buy at the price price I’ve seen it at in a while.

Interesting in dipping your toe in the world of local, agentic AI? I know that will sound cringey to some—and trust me, I get it. But there's no denying the increasing interest in using the Mac Mini for just that, and the latest M6 is particularly good at it, as I learned in my own testing. Of course, the M6 Mac Mini has a broader appeal too, and it's great to see it on sale so soon after launching. If you need even more performance for your AI curiosity, you'll need the Mac Studio, which also received its first discount since launching, coming in at $150 under its retail price.

Gaming laptops have gotten far too expensive recently, so I was delighted to see that one of my favorite gaming laptops to recommend has a huge sale. The price on this has fluctuated wildly over the past few months, but this deal on the RTX 5060 is the best I've seen in many months. The RTX 5060 grants you some pretty decent gaming performance, but the LOQ 15's higher-quality screen is better than every other gaming laptop in this price range. Also consider the RTX 5060 model for $1,399 at Walmart, which is cheaper but comes with half as much storage.

If you don’t want another subscription in your life, the Asus ZenWiFi BT10 is the best mesh system for you. You get three bands of stable Wi-Fi 7 coverage for your home. A two-pack will cover most properties (up to 6,000 square feet), there are two high-speed 10 Gbps ports (alongside a Gigabit LAN and USB 3.0), and security software, parental controls, and extras like VPN support are included. Clip the coupon for the lowest price here.

You won't find a better cheap monitor than this. That's always true of the Dell 27 Plus S2725HSM, but it's especially true at $130, which is the cheapest I've ever seen it at. It's just a basic 1920 x 1080 resolution, but the fully adjustable stand and great image quality gives this a major step up over every comparable monitor I've seen. If you've got some more cash to spend, I'd also recommend the upgraded 4K model, which is also on sale at a new low price.

A tidy, affordable pair of PC speakers, Edifier’s M60 is a bargain at its usual price, so this discount is not to be sniffed at. These speakers produce a surprisingly rich, clear sound that persists when you crank the volume, and there’s a thump of bass. They also come with angled stands, and connect via USB-C, 3.5 mm, or Bluetooth 5.3.

Tablets and E-Reader Deals

The best iPad for most people, if you don’t already have the iPad (11th-generation, A16), now is the time to buy. The 11-inch screen is perfect for kicking back on the couch with a book, game, or movie. It has a pair of 12-megapixel cameras, and Touch ID in the power button. It’s also handy for keeping the kids amused.

Fancy an e-reader that can also serve as a digital notebook? Amazon’s third-generation Kindle Scribe has you covered. It’s slim, with an 11-inch screen, smart stylus, and a bunch of AI features. It’s a go-to choice for note-takers and students. While we recommend the older model in our best Kindles guide, that’s mainly due to the lower price, and this is a better option when it’s on sale. Such as right now.

This 10.9-inch is currently out top pick for the best Android tablet you can buy. Just barely sliding in cheaper than the 11-inch iPad, the Galaxy Tab S10 FE makes for a brilliant alternative. Unlike the iPad, the Galaxy Tab S10 FE comes with an included S Pen stylus for notetaking, 8 GB of memory (instead of the iPad's 6 GB), as well as a faster 90-Hz refresh rate display. If you need a larger display, the 13.1-inch Galaxy Tab S10 FE+ is also on sale, though it's a bit heavier.

Home Tech Deals

If you’re looking for an easy security system and you don’t mind paying a pricey subscription ($10 per month or $96 a year for a single camera, $20 per month or $216 a year for unlimited cameras), Arlo is the way to go. This outdoor camera captures 2K video, has a 160-degree field of view, two-way audio, and direct Wi-Fi connection. It’s the best of the best outdoor security cameras. The Arlo app is fast, with rich notifications and two-factor authentication, so you can log in with your fingerprint or face, phone permitting.

If you can't stomach another subscription, this is the best subscription-free camera for most people, and this is a decent discount. It combines a triple-lens setup with a 4K fixed main lens that has a 130-degree field of view, and dual 2K lenses that pan through 360 degrees and tilt through 70 degrees. There's also a 10,000-mAh battery with a solar panel, onboard AI, and 32 GB of storage.

Combining a white noise machine, sunrise alarm light, and clock into a single device designed to help lull you to sleep and wake you gently, Hatch’s third generation Restore is an all-in-one way to establish a healthy sleep routine. It also enables you to leave your phone outside the bedroom. It’s annoying that you need a subscription to unlock all the content, but if it helps you get a better night’s sleep, it’s worth it.

If you like to stay organized, this 27-inch smart calendar could be for you. You can sync calendars, organize your meal plans, create to-do lists, and see your family’s day-to-day laid out in a clear format. Smart calendars might not be worth it for everyone, and some features require a subscription (digital photo frame functionality, smart assistant, rewards), but this is a decent discount on the biggest model.

Price increases this year across tech products have been demoralizing, but that's the beauty of Prime Day. The latest Amazon Echo Dot is back to $40, a full 50 percent discount from its retail price. This puts it awfully close to the prices it was selling for earlier this year. Not only does the Echo Dot do all the standard smart speaker stuff, it even acts as a mesh Wi-Fi extender to spread more connectivity through your space

entries.title: Tropical Storm Isaias Set to Be First Atlantic Hurricane of 2026 Season
entries.summary: Tropical Storm Isaias is set to become the basin’s first hurricane of the season, bringing life-threatening rain and storm surge to the Gulf Coast.
entries.content:
The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has been mercifully dull, but that’s set to change this week. Tropical Storm Isaias is forecast to become the season’s first hurricane before making landfall somewhere between Mississippi and Florida by the weekend.

El Niño has turned the Atlantic basin into a graveyard by changing winds high in the atmosphere so that they rip apart storms. That’s helped depress tropical cyclone activity to near-record-low levels and resulted in zero hurricanes. That could change imminently, though.

Isaias is churning in the Gulf of Mexico with winds of 65 mph, according to the latest update from the US National Hurricane Center. That’s just a shade below hurricane strength. The storm is forecast to pass over a patch of abnormally warm water, providing fuel for it to blossom into a hurricane. It could peak as a Category 2 storm with winds of 110 mph as it lumbers to the northeast. The storm is expected to weaken due to those aforementioned gnarly winds shortly before it makes landfall somewhere along the Gulf Coast.

The NHC has issued hurricane watches for all the coastline in Mississippi and Alabama as well as parts of the Florida Panhandle. (Tropical storm watches extend into Louisiana as well.)

Folks in that region can expect rainfall totals of up to 7 inches, though some spots in the Panhandle could see as much as 10 inches and storm surge as high as 7 feet. Tornadoes aren’t out of the question either. In other words, it’s a storm to take seriously.

Isaias could make also (or at least tie) history as the latest first Atlantic hurricane to form on record. The current record was set in 1905, when the season’s first hurricane formed on October 8. There’s still one more update scheduled for Isaias on Wednesday, so it’s possible it could just miss out on tying that mark.

Record or not, Isaias is indicative of the hurricane season that wasn’t. This year’s Atlantic hurricane season was forecast to be below average. But it’s been even quieter than expected owing to an El Niño that’s been dubbed “super,” “Godzilla,” and “supersized.” The superlatives—which meteorologists will be quick to tell you are not official designations—are indicative of the strength of this year’s event. El Niño is measured by ocean temperatures in a part of the tropical Pacific, and this year’s iteration has seen record highs throughout the summer and first part of fall.

The intensity has had a heavy hand in rearranging the atmosphere around the world, including over the Atlantic. Saharan dust has also played a role in quieting things by making the air in one of the major areas where hurricanes develop too damn dry.

For a sense of how that has impacted the Atlantic hurricane season, we can look at some averages. From 1991 to 2020, the basin saw an average of 14 named storms, seven hurricanes, and three major hurricanes—that is, storms of Category 3 or greater—annually, according to NHC data. This year has seen eight tropical storms and one soon-to-be hurricane.

Another metric to measure the season is accumulated cyclone energy (ACE for short), which takes into account not just the number and intensity of storms but how long they stick around. The ACE to date for 2026 is 10.8 units. The average for this time of year? Nearly 102, according to data maintained by Colorado State University. Most of that energy typically accumulates from mid-August through late September.

None of this is to say there might not be another surprise storm in the coming weeks. But with El Niño continuing to intensify and the peak of the season well past, the odds of this season seeing a sudden spurt of activity are minimal at best.

entries.title: Shaq Got Hacked. Now He’s Pitching for a VPN
entries.summary: At a recent event for security firm NordVPN, NBA superstar Shaquille O’Neal revealed that he got hacked—and warned the public about the need to “have control of their own information.”
entries.content:
At a promotional event in Times Square on Wednesday for the security company NordVPN, brand ambassador Shaquille O’Neal said he is eager to raise awareness among regular people about the importance of digital security and personal privacy.

“I have a video of me beating up Charles Barkley, and I wouldn't want the world to see that. That was a joke,” O'Neal says. “But everybody needs to have control of their own information.”

After being targeted by scammers who claimed that he was trying to buy a house and they were working on the transaction, O’Neal says, he realized he needed to learn more about cybersecurity and digital defense.

“I was hacked for the first time, not a bad hack, and I didn't know what to do,” he told reporters. “So I had to look into it. Once that happened, I really had to start paying more attention, because I would think nothing like that could ever happen to me, but it could happen to anybody.”

O'Neal, of course, is not just anybody. Still, the four-time NBA champion and media personality says that he doesn't have particularly sensitive data on his devices and tries to live a normal life as much as possible. When WIRED asked, though, whether he worries that he needs to take extra precautions to protect himself and loved ones as a result of his high profile, O'Neal said, “Yes, I think about it all the time, but I don't let it consume me, because if you let it consume you you can go crazy. But you have to be able to have great reactionary skills if something happens.”

A prolific tech investor who was early to AI, O'Neal emphasizes that the goal of his relationship with NordVPN is to inform the public and help people protect themselves. NordVPN is, well, known for its VPN. But the company has other offerings, including antivirus, threat detection, and scam-defense products that are geared toward accessibility for consumers. Marijus Briedis, the company's chief technology officer, says he was surprised by the findings of a recent NordVPN poll showing that 73 percent of Americans have an overconfidence in traditional antivirus and believe it can protect them against anything from identity theft to online tracking.

“The weakest link is between the computer and the chair, and I've been thinking so much about how to solve that problem,” Briedis told WIRED. “So the thing we are doing right now is focusing on education. It's a really interesting problem, how to do it in the best way. It's still haunting me in my dreams.”

entries.title: Best Prime Day Vacuum Deals: Save Big On a Dyson (2026)
entries.summary: I’ve compared cordless sticks, watched robot vacuums chase stains, and cleaned plenty of car crumbs. These discounts get my recommendation.

A good vacuum will seriously improve your life and home. So don't skip past Amazon's Prime Day vacuum deals before the event ends; instead, let me show you the best ones.

As WIRED's resident vacuum expert and tester, I've tried dozens of vacuums this year, from cordless sticks and Dysons to robot vacuums. (At one point this summer, there were at least 13 different vacuums in my home for testing!) I have persuaded everyone in my life to upgrade and can report no regrets from anyone who has followed my advice. One of my friends calls her robot vacuum her marriage-saver, while another friend loves hers so much she bought one for each floor of her home. Upgrading your stick vacuum can also make a huge difference—I had a friend test the new Dyson V8 Cyclone against her old V8 she's had for years, and she could immediately tell a difference.

This could be you! Especially if you choose from one of the vacuums I've personally vetted. Note that these deals for Prime Day—or, as Amazon's fall event is now named, Prime Big Deal Days—only include vacuums we've tested and recommend even when they aren't on sale.

While you're here, don't miss our story on the Absolute Best Prime Day Deals that we're keeping live the rest of today, plus our Prime Day liveblog.

entries.title: Elon Musk’s America PAC Is Quietly Funding November’s Most Consequential Elections
entries.summary: America PAC’s approach has been unusual: for every dollar it has spent supporting GOP Senate candidates, it has spent almost three dollars attacking Democrats.
entries.content:
Elon Musk’s America PAC is focusing its war chest on the most consequential Senate races this midterm cycle—and doing so by financing attack ads on Democrats, as voters nationwide sour on the Trump administration’s agenda.

The trend of political parties and outside groups focusing on trashing their opponents is not a new phenomenon. But America PAC's approach has been unusual: for every dollar it has spent supporting GOP Senate candidates, it has spent almost three dollars attacking Democrats.

To monitor America PAC's spending ​on digital ads and mailers this cycle, our ace team at WIRED has created a live tracker that updates daily and highlights where Musk's political contributions are heading as we enter the waning years of Trump’s second term.

The political stakes are especially high for Republicans this midterms cycle because of the possibility of Democrats taking the majority in the US Senate, should the party flip four battleground races and retain three of the Senate seats it currently holds.

For Musk, the implications of a Democratic-controlled Senate would also be far-reaching, as he personally could become the target of congressional investigations, while his companies might be affected by bills related to tech and AI regulation.

Texas Senate Race

For the critical Texas Senate race, America PAC has poured more than $9.4 million into ads opposing Democratic candidate James Talarico and roughly $1.8 million into ads backing Republican candidate and ​state ​attorney ​general Ken Paxton​.

The lopsided spending here is perhaps the least surprising of all of the close Senate contests. ​Paxton comes with so much personal baggage—from facing impeachment charges that were eventually dropped to having his wife (who has since endorsed him with an ad that doesn’t mention him by name) file for divorce on “biblical grounds”—that trying to boost him with ads highlighting his background is tough.

Republicans in Texas also cannot realistically do positive ads of President Donald Trump and Paxton together, since both men have terrible approval ratings.

The largest single expenditures by America PAC have been two $1.3 million digital media buys opposing Talarico. America PAC has not put any money into television ads, which is being handled by other groups, like MAGA Inc., the Trump-affiliated super PAC.

Meanwhile, the Senate Republican Conference–affiliated Texas PAC has so far booked the lion's share of television ads. Punchbowl News reported last month that Texas PAC has booked around $120 million and was looking to buy $100 million in ad slots before November 3.

Ohio Senate Race

In Ohio’s Senate race, America PAC has spent $3.3 million against Democrat Sherrod Brown compared to $1.6 million supporting Republican candidate Jon Husted.

Husted has been struggling to distance himself from supporting data centers at a time when voters in the state have become fed up with rising costs associated with the projects. Husted has been tagged as "the face of data centers" because of a planned Nvidia data center project in Ohio that will be leased by OpenAI, and for his past support for data centers when he served in the state government.

The effort by Brown to cast Husted as the champion of data centers has in fact been so effective that a memo by the Senate Republicans' campaign arm in August said it was tying an anchor around the neck of Husted's public polling.

At a rally this week in Ohio, despite the cratering public support for data centers, Trump could not help himself and declared to the crowd: “We want them.” Husted’s campaign quickly replied that it should be a “local decision.”

Iowa Senate Race

In Iowa, America PAC has spent $1.5 million hitting Democratic candidate Josh Turek, while only spending roughly $100,000 supporting the Republican candidate Ashley Hinson—the biggest disparity, according to the WIRED tracker.

To put that another way: To date, Musk's political operation has spent a staggering 14 times more attacking Turek than supporting Hinson.

This could be because Hinson has taken great pains to distance herself from Trump's agenda. She recently called on Trump to ban diesel exports and end the Iran war (after previously voting six times against the House resolution to end the conflict), after Turek called for both of those measures.

To illustrate the upside-down nature of this race, Hinson recently launched attack ads against Turek, accusing him without evidence of having “received tens of millions in support from men in the Epstein files,” a remarkable situation given that Trump has sought to tamp down any mention of the files because of the negative blowback on him personally.

Once again, pro-Republican ads are likely not helpful when the candidate is trying to run a race apart from Trump and is barely ahead in the polls in what should be a safe Republican seat. In the most recent New York Times/Siena poll, Hinson was just one single, solitary point ahead of Turek.

This is an edition of Hugo Lowell’s Inner Loop newsletter. Read previous newsletters here.

entries.title: The Science Behind the Nobel-Winning Technology That Controls Neurons With Light
entries.summary: Optogenetics revolutionized neuroscience, but its origins come from an entirely brainless organism—an alga.
entries.content:
The Karolinska Institute awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Medicine to researchers Karl Deisseroth of Stanford University, Peter Hegemann of Humboldt University in Berlin, and Georg Nagel of the University of Würzburg. Their discoveries led to the development of optogenetics, a technique where scientists can turn individual nerve cells on or off using beams of light.

According to Per Svenningsson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Medicine, “Optogenetics provides opportunities for mapping the brain in a way that we could once only dream of.” No other technique allows for such precise study of a living brain, helping researchers better understand the functions of our nervous systems as well as various neurological diseases and disorders.

But this prize is not just a celebration of neuroscience. It also serves as a triumphant example of what can happen when different disciplines of biology converge, as the findings that served as the basis for the development of optogenetics emerged from research in microbiology.

At the end of the last century, Peter Hegemann began a series of studies to understand how the single-celled alga Chlamydomonas is able to detect and react to light. Previous research documented that Chlamydomonas has an “eye spot,” a small orange dot on its surface that contains a light-sensing molecule called retinal.

Hegemann used tiny electrodes to measure the electrical signals generated by the alga and to expand our understanding of this structure’s rapid response. The scientist discovered that the organism was capable of producing an electrical impulse about 0.5 milliseconds after receiving light. This response time is 20 times faster than that of the human eye, whose light detection process takes at least 10 milliseconds.

Hegemann suggested that light detection in the alga must be the result of a much simpler process than that identified in the human eye. In the early 1990s, he proposed that the eye spots contained a protein that both detected the light and responded to it, likely opening as a channel to let ions through. At the time, this hypothesis sparked controversy. Many ion channels had been documented up to that point, but none could respond to light on their own.

To test his theory, the scientist attempted to isolate the light-sensitive proteins from the eye spot. However, when removed from their natural environment, these proteins became unstable. Later, a group of Japanese researchers sequenced the complete DNA of Chlamydomonas, which allowed Hegemann’s team to identify two genes that would create proteins with the expected characteristics of a possible light-sensing channel.

Georg Nagel took the next step of verifying the function of the genes. He introduced copies of each of the identified genes separately into different groups of frog eggs. The eggs began to produce the corresponding proteins, which eventually localized to the cell membranes. Nagel then turned on the lights.

Both proteins functioned as ion channels that opened when exposed to light. He named the genes channelrhodopsin-1 and channelrhodopsin-2. Further experiments showed the protein produced by this second gene—called ChR2 for short—opened especially quickly, the flow of ions occurring in just 0.2 milliseconds. It explained the extraordinary speed of the light reaction originally observed in Chlamydomonas.

When the researchers introduced the gene into mammalian cells—which do not normally respond to light—the cells generated an electrical signal when illuminated. This is what got the neuroscientists particularly excited.

Ion channels are important across many types of cells, but they do some especially heavy lifting in our nervous systems. The electrical impulses that neurons use to communicate with one another, as well as other tissues in our body, are mediated by the flow of ions in and out of the cell. If you can control the ion channels, you can control the neuron.

This is where Karl Deisseroth comes in. Deisseroth was searching for a method that would allow him to toggle the activity of specific nerve cells in a living brain. In his view, this tool could expand our understanding of brain functions and open new avenues for treating conditions such as depression and schizophrenia.

Following the discovery of ChR2, he asked Nagel for the DNA sequence so he could introduce it into rat nerve cells. The neurons, growing in dishes, produced ChR2 and, when illuminated with blue light, reacted immediately—sending an electrical impulse that propagated to other neurons. This result, obtained in 2005, was decisive in establishing ChR2 as a tool for neuroscience.

In the following years, Deisseroth, Hegemann, and Nagel collaborated to identify other proteins capable of activating or deactivating neurons using different wavelengths of light. With this toolkit, researchers can now design experiments where one group of neurons is turned on by one wavelength of light and another set of neurons is controlled by a different wavelength.

The term optogenetics was coined in 2006 and has since been implemented in a variety of studies. “Using optogenetics, researchers have been able to reveal neural circuits governing specific memories, feelings, and behaviors relevant for neurological and psychiatric disorders. In clinical medicine, researchers are using the method in attempts to restore sight in people with visual impairment,” the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institute stated in a press release.

This story originally appeared on WIRED en Español and has been translated from Spanish.
